title: Fish by Melis Aker at WP Theatre #fishplay #wptheater #signaturetheat...
transcript: Sexting terrorists is one way to look for your missing brother — teenagers are so creative. In this new dark comedy, playwright Melis Aker uses a strikingly unique story to explore universal teenage experiences. Sandwiched by an uncontrollably anxious mother and a best friend who's preoccupied with her new boyfriend, Karya barely has time to process her own life. Her brother has been missing for some time now, and one of the leading theories puts her down a dangerous but amusing path which involves dm-ing terrorists. What I enjoyed the most about this show, other than the way it nails the comedic awkwardness of adolescence, is how it quietly builds emotional tension underneath an entertaining plot. It sneaks up on you, and you don't realize how much emotional subtext is going on until the climax, which is a moment of clarity for Karya, but not in the way you'd expect. It all clicks in a way that's very show, not tell. Karya and her mom don't really dig into what the brother being missing has done to them, it just manifests in their behavior. I actually wish we'd gotten more of the mom character, though she doesn't propel the narrative as much as Karya's friend Libby. I will say the dynamic between them is really funny and is what makes the piece feel relatable, despite its more outlandish plot points. But the most relatable part of the show is how it captures the suffocating teenage feeling of life swallowing you whole, much to the credit of lead actress Yasmin Ranz-Lind.
reasoning: Reviewer praises the comedic writing, emotional subtext, and lead performance, with only a minor wish for more of the mom character. Clear recommendation but measured in tone rather than ecstatic.
keyQuote: it quietly builds emotional tension underneath an entertaining plot
